method: Read690 additional contiguous source lines: shell icons, eviction and paint back-buffer. Static resource-lifecycle analysis only.
findings: Owned icon cache limit is implemented: while count exceeds256 remove an arbitrary HashSet key excluding keep, remove map entry and DestroyIcon. This resolves earlier declaration-only uncertainty. It is not LRU; receiver passes empty keep, so freshly inserted icon can be evicted. No cache-hit benchmark.

Failed icon channel send leaves key in pending_icons because insert precedes unchecked send; subsequent requests skip pending key. Successful null icon response removes pending and does not negative-cache, allowing future retry.

WINDOW icons are cached separately without marking owned; borrowed-versus-owned lifetime depends on unread get_window_icon helper. Do not free all cached icons indiscriminately or claim all are leaks.

Back-buffer growth deletes previous bitmap while it remains selected into previous memory DC, then deletes DC and loses bitmap handle. Actual DeleteObject result ignored; Windows selected-object deletion behavior needs platform fixture. Source ordering risks resource leak on grow.

Back-buffer records requested size and new handles without checking compatible DC/bitmap creation. Failed bitmap allocation with nonnull DC can leave cache considered large enough for reuse. No fault-injection runtime control.

Back-buffer intentionally grows but never shrinks and has no explicit Drop cleanup or display-format invalidation; source comments disclose retained exit resources. No process memory/GDI counts measured.

App-path registry helper uses fixed256UTF16 buffer and no retry on larger values; supported type only REG_SZ. Successful query closes handle before type/path validation; failed query closes too. No registry handles accessed in review.
App-icon modern path releases image bitmap and mask after CreateIconIndirect; legacy PIDL path releases PIDL. This normal ownership handling must be distinguished from independent back-buffer issue.
Filesystem existence checks happen in icon classification on UI request path and again worker path. No latency or performance improvement claim from reading alone.
limits: No tests/GDI/registry/runtime actions or local production changes.
